agent.result_text:
The implementation is complete and the full test suite is green.

## Summary

The spec required locality derivation to **prefer the postcode** over the city. I modified `getLocality()` in `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`:

1. **Added a `REGION_POSTCODES` map** — the inclusive 4-digit ranges per region (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099).

2. **Rewrote `getLocality()`** to look up the region by postcode range first via a new `regionForPostcode(...)` helper, and only fall back to the existing `CITY_REGION` city table when the postcode is absent, not exactly 4 digits, or in no known range. Updated the Javadoc on all three members to match.

Why this is safe for existing behavior: in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`, `validatePostcode(...)` is called with `owner.getLocality()` *before* `owner.setPostcode(...)` runs, so at validation time the postcode is still null and locality remains city-derived — existing postcode-range validation is unchanged. The stored postcode only drives the locality on read-back.

Test results:
- `coreRegionFromPostcodeRange` — Sydney + postcode 2000 → `NSW` ✅ (same region for known cities)
- `functionalityPostcodePreferredOverCity` — unknown city + postcode 3000 → `VIC` ✅ (postcode disambiguates)
- Full suite: **Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0 — BUILD SUCCESS**

probe.probe_text:
POST `/api/owners` is handled by `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner(...)` (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java:184`). Here is everything that happens, in order.

## Before the method body runs

1. **Authorization** — `@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")` (line 182): the caller must hold the `OWNER_ADMIN` role, or the request is rejected before any logic runs.
2. **Bean Validation of the request body** — the `OwnerFieldsDto` is validated by the framework (`@Valid` on the generated `OwnersApi`) against its field constraints (e.g. `@NotEmpty`/`@Size`/`@Pattern`) before the controller method is entered.

## Inside `addOwner`, in order

1. **`validateRequiredFields(...)`** (line 185) — rejects a missing/blank `firstName`, `lastName`, `address` (checked *after* `normalizeAddress`, so whitespace/empty collapses to blank), `city`, or `telephone`. Any offending fields are collected and thrown together as `InvalidOwnerFieldsException` → **400**.
2. **Compute the registration date** (lines 186–187) — take the supplied `registrationDate`, or `LocalDate.now()` if absent, then **`toBusinessDay(...)`** rolls a Saturday/Sunday forward to the next Monday. (Side-effect: the effective date is adjusted; this adjusted date feeds the daily-limit bucket and the stored value.)
3. **`rejectDailyLimitReached(registrationDate)`** (line 188) — if **≥ 100** existing owners already carry that (business-day) registration date, throw `DailyOwnerLimitReachedException` → **429**.
4. **Map DTO → `Owner`** (line 190) via `ownerMapper.toOwner(...)`.
5. **Normalize & set address** (lines 191–192) — `normalizeAddress(...)`: trim, collapse internal whitespace, upper-case, and expand whole-token street abbreviations (`ST`→`STREET`, `RD`→`ROAD`, `AVE`→`AVENUE`). (Side-effect: stored/returned address is the normalized form.)
6. **`rejectCityAtCapacity(owner.getCity())`** (line 193) — if the city already holds **≥ 50** owners (counted case-/whitespace-insensitively), throw `OwnerCityAtCapacityException` → **409**.
7. **Household assignment** (lines 194–196) — only if `sharesHousehold == true`: `assignHousehold(...)` finds existing owners sharing the (normalized) last name + address; if any exist, every member and the new owner get the same `householdId` (reusing an existing one, else deriving a SHA-256-based `HH-<HEX12>` id). (Side-effect: back-fills and **persists existing owner records** via `saveOwner`, and sets the new owner's `householdId`.)
8. **Normalize & set telephone** (lines 197–198) — `normalizeTelephone(...)`: strip spaces/dashes/brackets, convert to E.164 (default `+61`, drop a leading national `0`), require `+` followed by 8–15 digits, and enforce the per-country national-number length (`+61`→9, `+1`→10). Invalid → `InvalidOwnerFieldsException` → **400**. (Side-effect: stored telephone is the E.164 form.)
9. **Normalize & set email** (lines 199–200) — `normalizeEmail(...)`: `null` is allowed (left unset); otherwise it must match the email pattern, and is stored **lower-cased**. Invalid → `InvalidOwnerFieldsException` → **400**.
10. **Validate & set postcode** (line 201) — `validatePostcode(...)`: `null` allowed; otherwise must be exactly 4 digits, and if the owner's locality (derived from city) has a known range (NSW 2000–2099, VIC 3000–3099, QLD 4000–4099) it must fall within it. Invalid → `InvalidOwnerFieldsException` → **400**.
11. **`rejectDuplicateIdentity(owner)`** (line 202) — build the identity key `telephone|email|householdId`; if any existing owner has the same key, throw `DuplicateOwnerIdentityException` → **409**.
12. **Set registration date** (line 203) — store the adjusted business-day date computed in step 2.
13. **Set namesake count** (line 204) — `countNamesakes(...)`: number of existing owners sharing the same (normalized) first + last name.
14. **Set customer code** (line 205) — `generateCustomerCode(...)`: `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`, where NNNN is a per-city sequence = (existing owners in city) + 1.
15. **Persist the owner** (line 206) — `clinicService.saveOwner(owner)`. At this point the `Owner` entity's own Bean Validation constraints also apply: `@NotEmpty` on `address`, `city`, `telephone`, and `@Pattern` requiring telephone in E.164 form.
16. **Audit log** (lines 207–208) — the `AUDIT` logger emits a line with the new owner's `id`, `customerCode`, and `registrationDate`. (Side-effect: audit log entry.)
17. **Build response DTO + bulk-signup warning** (lines 209–210) — map to `OwnerDto` and `applyBulkSignupWarning(...)` sets `bulkSignupWarning = true` when **more than 80** owners already carry today's business-day registration date.
18. **Set `Location` header & return** (lines 211–213) — `Location: /api/owners/{id}`, response **201 Created** with the owner body.

Note: V2 (`OwnerRestControllerV2`) exposes only a paged list; it has no create endpoint, so all POST `/api/owners` creation logic is the V1 path above.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The change fits the existing structure of `Owner` cleanly:

- The class already holds a sibling static lookup table (`CITY_REGION`) backing a `@Transient` derived getter, so adding `REGION_POSTCODES` as a second constant table in the same spot is consistent and additive, not a new concern bolted on.
- Locality derivation already lives on the `Owner` model; the postcode-preference logic belongs in the same unit as the fallback it extends. No logic leaked into a controller/service or anywhere unnatural.
- Extracting `regionForPostcode` as a private static helper keeps `getLocality()` readable (prefer-then-fallback stays a two-step read) rather than inlining the parse/range loop — matching how the other derived getters here stay focused.
- No duplication: the city table is reused as-is for the fallback path, and the Javadoc on both the field and getter was updated to reflect the new precedence rather than left stale.
- `Owner` is already the home for several derived `@Transient` values (`getMembershipNumber`, `getIdentityKey`, `getContactPreference`), so this isn't tipping a previously-cohesive class into catch-all territory — it's one more derivation of the same kind.

A maintainer of this codebase would find this natural.
